source_text:
Δίκαιον οὖν καὶ ὅσιον, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ὑπηκόους ἡμᾶς μᾶλλον γενέσθαι τῷ θεῷ ἡ τοῖς ἐν ἀλαζονείᾳ καὶ ἀκαταστασίᾳ μυσεροῦ ζήλους ἀρχηγοῖς ἐξακολουθεῖν.
βλάβην γὰρ οὐ τὴν τυχοῦσαν, μᾶλλον δὲ κίνδυνον ὑποίσομεν μέγαν, ἐὰν ῥιψοκινδύνως ἐπιδῶμεν ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς θελήμασιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, οἵτινες ἐξακοντίζουσιν εἰς ἔριν καὶ στάσεις, εἰς τὸ ἀπαλλοτριῶσαι ἡμᾶς τοῦ καλῶς ἔχοντος.
χρηστευσώμεθα ἑαυτοῖς κατὰ τὴν εὐσπλαγχνίαν καὶ γλυκύτητα τοῦ ποιήσαντος ἡμᾶς.
γέγραπται γάρ: Χρηστοὶ ἔσονται οἰκήτορες γῆς, ἄκακοι δὲ ὑπολειφθήσονται ἐπ αὐτῆς: οἱ δὲ παρανομοῦντες ἐξολεθρευθήσονται ἀπ’ αὐτῆς.
καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Εἶδον ἀσεβῆ ὑπερυψούμενον καὶ ἐπαιρόμενον ὡς τὰς κέδρους τοῦ Λιβάνου: καὶ παρῆλθον, καὶ ἰδοὺ οὐκ ἦν, καὶ ἐξεζήτησα τὸν τόπον αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐχ εὗρον. φύλασσε ἀκακίαν καὶ ἴδε εὐθύτητα, ὅτι ἐστὶν ἐγκατάλειμμα ἀνθρώπῳ εἰρηνικῷ.
thought_title: Obey God rather than leaders of envy
orientation: The writer from Rome urges the Corinthians to obey God rather than follow the few who stir envy and faction against the elders.
pass_a_gloss: It is just therefore and holy, men who are brothers, for us to become obedient to God rather than to follow the leaders of hateful envy in arrogance and disorder. For we will sustain harm not of the ordinary kind, but rather great danger, if recklessly we give over ourselves to the purposes of the men who hurl us into strife and factions, so as to alienate us from that which is good. Let us act kindly toward ourselves according to the compassion and sweetness of the one who made us. For it stands written: Kind people will be inhabitants of land, and innocent people will be left remaining upon it, but those who break the law will be destroyed from it. And again it says: I saw an impious man being lifted high and exalted like the cedars of Lebanon, and I passed by, and behold he was not, and I sought his place, and I did not find it. Guard innocence and see uprightness, because there is a remnant for a peaceable man.

WORK BRIEF glossary fixes στάσις as faction for the Corinthian division
literal vocative address, keeping both nouns without polishing to brothers alone

choices.why: literal rendering of remnant and peaceable man, preserving the promise to the innocent
rejected: a future for the man of peace

pass_b_english: So it is right and holy, men who are brothers, for us to obey God rather than follow the leaders of hateful envy in their arrogance and disorder.

For we will suffer no ordinary harm. On the contrary, we will face great danger if we recklessly hand ourselves over to the wishes of people who drive us into strife and factions to estrange us from what is good. Let us be kind to one another, in keeping with the compassion and gentleness of the one who made us.

For it is written: "The upright will dwell in the land, and the innocent will be left in it, but the lawless will be destroyed from it" (Proverbs 2:21-22). And again Scripture says: "I saw the wicked exalted and lifted high like the cedars of Lebanon, and I passed by, and behold, he was gone, and I sought his place and did not find it. Keep innocence and look to uprightness, for there is a remnant for a peaceable man" (Psalm 37:35-37).

last_rejected.quote: For we will suffer no ordinary harm. On the contrary, we will face great danger if we recklessly hand ourselves over
last_rejected.source_quote: βλάβην γὰρ οὐ τὴν τυχοῦσαν, μᾶλλον δὲ κίνδυνον ὑποίσομεν μέγαν, ἐὰν ῥιψοκινδύνως ἐπιδῶμεν ἑαυτοὺς
last_rejected.why: One conditional verb governs both objects. English states the harm as certain and conditions only the danger.
last_rejected.fix: For we will suffer no ordinary harm, but rather great danger, if we recklessly hand ourselves over to the wishes of such people.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek 'ὑποίσομεν' is future indicative governing both objects; 'ἐὰν...ἐπιδῶμεν' conditions the whole clause. English 'we will suffer no ordinary harm... great danger if' is a natural, harmless rendering.
